label: Renal
blurb: Diuretics, electrolyte and acid-base agents, CKD therapy, gout drugs

drugs.name: Furosemide
drugs.primaryEffect: Produces the most potent diuresis of any diuretic class
drugs.treatmentUsage: Acute decompensated heart failure, pulmonary edema, volume overload in chronic kidney disease, hypercalcemia, refractory hypertension
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits the Na-K-2Cl cotransporter in the thick ascending limb, abolishing the medullary concentration gradient and preventing reabsorption of up to 25 percent of filtered sodium.
drugs.sideEffects: Hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, hypocalcemia, metabolic alkalosis, ototoxicity, hyperuricemia and gout, hyperglycemia, sulfa allergy cross-reactivity
drugs.contraindications: Anuria, severe electrolyte depletion, hepatic coma, sulfa allergy (use ethacrynic acid instead)
drugs.tooltip: Loops lose calcium; thiazides retain it. That distinction drives two exam questions: furosemide for hypercalcemia, thiazides for calcium stones. Ethacrynic acid is the non-sulfa alternative.

drugs.name: Bumetanide
drugs.primaryEffect: Potent diuresis with more reliable oral absorption
drugs.treatmentUsage: Heart failure with gut edema impairing furosemide absorption, refractory volume overload, nephrotic syndrome
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Blocks the Na-K-2Cl cotransporter in the thick ascending limb, producing natriuresis and diuresis identical in mechanism to furosemide but with roughly 40-fold greater potency per milligram.
drugs.sideEffects: Hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, metabolic alkalosis, ototoxicity, hyperuricemia, muscle cramps
drugs.contraindications: Anuria, hepatic coma, severe electrolyte depletion, sulfa allergy
drugs.tooltip: Chosen over furosemide when gut wall edema makes oral furosemide absorption erratic, since bumetanide bioavailability is consistently near 80 to 100 percent.

drugs.name: Hydrochlorothiazide
drugs.primaryEffect: Mild diuresis with sustained blood pressure reduction
drugs.treatmentUsage: Hypertension, calcium-containing kidney stone prevention, nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, mild edema, osteoporosis adjunct
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits the Na-Cl cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule, reducing sodium reabsorption; enhanced distal calcium reabsorption follows from the altered electrochemical gradient.
drugs.sideEffects: Hypokalemia, hyponatremia, hypercalcemia, hyperuricemia and gout, hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia, pancreatitis, photosensitivity, sulfa cross-reactivity
drugs.contraindications: Anuria, sulfa allergy, severe hyponatremia, symptomatic hyperuricemia; loses efficacy when eGFR falls below 30
drugs.tooltip: Thiazides cause hyperGLUC: hyperGlycemia, hyperLipidemia, hyperUricemia, hyperCalcemia. Paradoxically they treat nephrogenic diabetes insipidus by inducing mild volume depletion and enhancing proximal water reabsorption.

drugs.name: Chlorthalidone
drugs.primaryEffect: Long-acting blood pressure reduction
drugs.treatmentUsage: Hypertension, particularly when 24-hour blood pressure control is the goal; resistant hypertension
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits the distal convoluted tubule Na-Cl cotransporter with a half-life of 40 to 60 hours, giving more sustained natriuresis than hydrochlorothiazide.
drugs.sideEffects: Hypokalemia (more pronounced than hydrochlorothiazide), hyponatremia, hyperuricemia, hyperglycemia, hypercalcemia
drugs.contraindications: Anuria, sulfa allergy, severe electrolyte disturbance
drugs.tooltip: Preferred over hydrochlorothiazide in many guidelines because its long half-life gives better overnight control and it has stronger outcome trial evidence, at the cost of more hypokalemia.

drugs.name: Spironolactone
drugs.primaryEffect: Mild diuresis with potassium retention
drugs.treatmentUsage: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, primary hyperaldosteronism, cirrhotic ascites, resistant hypertension, hirsutism and acne in PCOS
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Competitively antagonizes the intracellular mineralocorticoid receptor in principal cells of the collecting duct, reducing ENaC and Na-K-ATPase expression so sodium is excreted and potassium retained.
drugs.sideEffects: Hyperkalemia, gynecomastia and breast tenderness, menstrual irregularity, metabolic acidosis, decreased libido
drugs.contraindications: Hyperkalemia, eGFR below 30, Addison disease, concurrent potassium supplementation or other potassium-sparing agents
drugs.tooltip: The diuretic of choice in cirrhotic ascites because secondary hyperaldosteronism drives the sodium retention. Its antiandrogen effect causes gynecomastia; eplerenone avoids this.

drugs.name: Eplerenone
drugs.primaryEffect: Selective aldosterone blockade without endocrine side effects
drugs.treatmentUsage: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, post-myocardial infarction left ventricular dysfunction, resistant hypertension, primary hyperaldosteronism
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Selectively antagonizes the mineralocorticoid receptor with far lower affinity for androgen and progesterone receptors than spironolactone.
drugs.sideEffects: Hyperkalemia, dizziness, elevated triglycerides, metabolic acidosis; minimal gynecomastia
drugs.contraindications: Hyperkalemia, eGFR below 30, concurrent strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ketoconazole or clarithromycin
drugs.tooltip: Chosen over spironolactone when gynecomastia or sexual side effects are unacceptable. It is a CYP3A4 substrate, so strong inhibitors are contraindicated.

drugs.name: Amiloride
drugs.primaryEffect: Blocks sodium reabsorption in the collecting duct without hormonal effects
drugs.treatmentUsage: Adjunct to thiazides or loops to prevent hypokalemia, Liddle syndrome, lithium-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, cystic fibrosis airway therapy historically
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Directly blocks the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) in the collecting duct principal cell apical membrane, reducing the lumen-negative potential that drives potassium and hydrogen secretion.
drugs.sideEffects: Hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis, nausea, headache; no antiandrogen effects
drugs.contraindications: Hyperkalemia, severe renal impairment, concurrent potassium supplements or aldosterone antagonists
drugs.tooltip: The treatment for Liddle syndrome, where a gain-of-function ENaC mutation causes hypertension with hypokalemia — spironolactone fails there because the defect is downstream of the receptor.

drugs.name: Acetazolamide
drugs.primaryEffect: Produces bicarbonate diuresis and metabolic acidosis
drugs.treatmentUsage: Glaucoma, acute mountain sickness prophylaxis, idiopathic intracranial hypertension, metabolic alkalosis correction, urinary alkalinization
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits carbonic anhydrase in the proximal tubule, preventing bicarbonate reabsorption so sodium bicarbonate is excreted; it also reduces aqueous humor and cerebrospinal fluid production.
drugs.sideEffects: Hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis, hypokalemia, paresthesias, calcium phosphate kidney stones, sulfa cross-reactivity, drowsiness
drugs.contraindications: Sulfa allergy, hepatic cirrhosis because of ammonia retention, hyperchloremic acidosis, severe renal or hepatic disease
drugs.tooltip: In altitude sickness the induced metabolic acidosis stimulates ventilation, speeding acclimatization. Self-limiting diuresis occurs because acidosis eventually reduces filtered bicarbonate.

drugs.name: Mannitol
drugs.primaryEffect: Draws water from tissues into the vascular space and increases urine output
drugs.treatmentUsage: Elevated intracranial pressure, cerebral edema, acute glaucoma, rhabdomyolysis-associated forced diuresis
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Freely filtered but not reabsorbed, it raises tubular fluid osmolality throughout the nephron so water reabsorption is impeded, and it osmotically pulls water from brain and eye tissue.
drugs.sideEffects: Initial volume expansion with pulmonary edema, subsequent hypovolemia, hypernatremia, hypokalemia, rebound intracranial pressure rise, acute kidney injury at high doses
drugs.contraindications: Anuria, established acute kidney injury, decompensated heart failure, active intracranial bleeding, severe dehydration
drugs.tooltip: Watch the biphasic volume effect: transient intravascular expansion that can flood a failing heart, then diuresis and hypovolemia. Serum osmolality and the osmolar gap guide dosing.

drugs.name: Tolvaptan
drugs.primaryEffect: Excretes free water while retaining sodium
drugs.treatmentUsage: Euvolemic and hypervolemic hyponatremia, SIADH, autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Blocks V2 receptors in the collecting duct so aquaporin-2 channels are not inserted, producing electrolyte-free water excretion known as aquaresis.
drugs.sideEffects: Thirst, polyuria, dry mouth, hepatotoxicity, overly rapid sodium correction causing osmotic demyelination
drugs.contraindications: Hypovolemic hyponatremia, anuria, inability to sense thirst, concurrent strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, urgent need to raise sodium rapidly
drugs.tooltip: In polycystic kidney disease it slows cyst growth because vasopressin-driven cAMP is the main driver of cyst expansion. Fluid restriction must be lifted during therapy to avoid overcorrection.

drugs.name: Patiromer
drugs.primaryEffect: Lowers serum potassium by increasing fecal excretion
drugs.treatmentUsage: Chronic hyperkalemia, especially to allow continued use of RAAS inhibitors in heart failure and chronic kidney disease
drugs.mechanismOfAction: A nonabsorbed polymer that exchanges calcium for potassium primarily in the distal colon, binding potassium for fecal elimination.
drugs.sideEffects: Constipation, diarrhea, hypomagnesemia, hypokalemia if overdosed, abdominal discomfort
drugs.contraindications: Bowel obstruction; separate from other oral medications by three hours because it binds them
drugs.tooltip: For chronic rather than emergency hyperkalemia — onset takes hours. Its real value is permitting ACE inhibitors and mineralocorticoid antagonists to be continued in heart failure.

drugs.name: Calcium Gluconate
drugs.primaryEffect: Immediately protects the myocardium from hyperkalemia
drugs.treatmentUsage: Hyperkalemia with ECG changes, hypocalcemia, calcium channel blocker overdose, magnesium toxicity, hydrofluoric acid burns
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Raises the extracellular calcium concentration, restoring the difference between resting and threshold potential in cardiac myocytes without changing serum potassium.
drugs.sideEffects: Tissue necrosis with extravasation, hypercalcemia, bradycardia with rapid infusion, vasodilation and hypotension
drugs.contraindications: Hypercalcemia, digoxin toxicity relative caution, ventricular fibrillation; do not mix with bicarbonate-containing solutions
drugs.tooltip: First drug in hyperkalemia with ECG changes. It does not lower potassium at all — it only stabilizes the myocardium while insulin, glucose, and albuterol shift potassium intracellularly.

drugs.name: Sodium Bicarbonate
drugs.primaryEffect: Raises serum and urine pH
drugs.treatmentUsage: Severe metabolic acidosis, tricyclic antidepressant and salicylate overdose, hyperkalemia with acidosis, urinary alkalinization, contrast nephropathy prophylaxis
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Provides bicarbonate that buffers hydrogen ions; in sodium channel blocker toxicity the sodium load plus alkalinization reduces drug binding to cardiac sodium channels.
drugs.sideEffects: Volume overload, hypernatremia, hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, hypocalcemia with tetany, paradoxical intracellular acidosis
drugs.contraindications: Metabolic or respiratory alkalosis, hypocalcemia, severe pulmonary edema, hypernatremia
drugs.tooltip: In tricyclic overdose, widened QRS is the indication and both the sodium load and the alkaline pH reduce drug binding to cardiac sodium channels. In salicylate overdose it traps salicylate in urine.

drugs.name: Allopurinol
drugs.primaryEffect: Lowers serum uric acid by blocking its production
drugs.treatmentUsage: Chronic gout prophylaxis, tumor lysis syndrome prevention, recurrent uric acid kidney stones, Lesch-Nyhan syndrome
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits xanthine oxidase, blocking conversion of hypoxanthine to xanthine and xanthine to uric acid, so more soluble precursors are excreted instead.
drugs.sideEffects: Rash, hypersensitivity syndrome with DRESS especially in HLA-B*5801 carriers, hepatotoxicity, acute gout flare on initiation, bone marrow suppression
drugs.contraindications: Concurrent azathioprine or 6-mercaptopurine without major dose reduction, prior severe hypersensitivity; test HLA-B*5801 in high-risk populations
drugs.tooltip: Never start during an acute flare without anti-inflammatory cover, since lowering urate mobilizes crystals. The azathioprine interaction is lethal: xanthine oxidase normally clears its active metabolite.

drugs.name: Febuxostat
drugs.primaryEffect: Potent reduction of serum uric acid
drugs.treatmentUsage: Chronic gout in patients intolerant of or unresponsive to allopurinol
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Selective non-purine inhibitor of both oxidized and reduced forms of xanthine oxidase, more potently blocking uric acid synthesis than allopurinol.
drugs.sideEffects: Increased cardiovascular mortality compared with allopurinol (boxed warning), elevated transaminases, rash, acute gout flare on initiation, nausea
drugs.contraindications: Established cardiovascular disease, concurrent azathioprine or 6-mercaptopurine
drugs.tooltip: Second-line because of the cardiovascular mortality signal from the CARES trial. It is hepatically cleared, so it does not require renal dose adjustment like allopurinol.

drugs.name: Colchicine
drugs.primaryEffect: Suppresses the inflammatory response to urate crystals
drugs.treatmentUsage: Acute gout flare, gout flare prophylaxis when starting urate-lowering therapy, familial Mediterranean fever, pericarditis
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Binds tubulin and prevents microtubule polymerization, impairing neutrophil chemotaxis, adhesion, and inflammasome-driven interleukin-1 beta release in response to crystals.
drugs.sideEffects: Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, myopathy and rhabdomyolysis, bone marrow suppression with overdose, peripheral neuropathy
drugs.contraindications: Severe renal or hepatic impairment with concurrent P-glycoprotein or CYP3A4 inhibitors such as clarithromycin, cyclosporine, or verapamil
drugs.tooltip: Low-dose regimens are as effective as old high-dose ones with far less diarrhea. Fatal toxicity occurs when combined with CYP3A4 or P-glycoprotein inhibitors in renal impairment.

drugs.name: Probenecid
drugs.primaryEffect: Increases renal uric acid excretion
drugs.treatmentUsage: Chronic gout in underexcretors of uric acid with preserved renal function; historically to prolong penicillin levels
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits the URAT1 transporter in the proximal tubule, blocking uric acid reabsorption; it also blocks organic anion secretion, which is why it raises penicillin levels.
drugs.sideEffects: Uric acid kidney stones, acute gout flare on initiation, rash, gastrointestinal upset, aplastic anemia rarely
drugs.contraindications: History of uric acid nephrolithiasis, overproduction of uric acid, creatinine clearance below 50 mL/min, concurrent aspirin which antagonizes it
drugs.tooltip: Requires a 24-hour urine uric acid to confirm underexcretion, plus high fluid intake and urinary alkalinization to prevent stones. Low-dose aspirin blocks its effect entirely.

drugs.name: Rasburicase
drugs.primaryEffect: Rapidly degrades existing uric acid
drugs.treatmentUsage: Tumor lysis syndrome prevention and treatment in high-risk hematologic malignancies
drugs.mechanismOfAction: A recombinant urate oxidase that converts uric acid to allantoin, which is five to ten times more water soluble and readily excreted; humans lack this enzyme naturally.
drugs.sideEffects: Severe hemolysis in G6PD deficiency, methemoglobinemia, anaphylaxis, falsely low uric acid readings in samples left at room temperature
drugs.contraindications: G6PD deficiency (absolute, must be screened), prior anaphylaxis to rasburicase
drugs.tooltip: Unlike allopurinol, which prevents new uric acid, rasburicase destroys uric acid already present, so it works in hours. Hydrogen peroxide is a byproduct, which is why G6PD deficiency causes hemolysis.

drugs.name: Epoetin Alfa
drugs.primaryEffect: Stimulates red blood cell production
drugs.treatmentUsage: Anemia of chronic kidney disease, chemotherapy-induced anemia, zidovudine-associated anemia, reduction of perioperative transfusion
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Recombinant erythropoietin that binds erythropoietin receptors on marrow erythroid progenitors, promoting their proliferation, differentiation, and survival.
drugs.sideEffects: Hypertension, increased thrombosis and stroke risk, tumor progression in some malignancies, pure red cell aplasia from anti-EPO antibodies, seizures
drugs.contraindications: Uncontrolled hypertension, hemoglobin target above 11 g/dL because of cardiovascular harm, pure red cell aplasia after prior use
drugs.tooltip: Targeting normal hemoglobin increases death, stroke, and thrombosis, so the target is deliberately subnormal. Iron stores must be repleted first or the drug will not work.

drugs.name: Sevelamer
drugs.primaryEffect: Reduces serum phosphate without a calcium load
drugs.treatmentUsage: Hyperphosphatemia in chronic kidney disease stages 4 and 5 and in dialysis patients
drugs.mechanismOfAction: A nonabsorbed cationic polymer that binds dietary phosphate anions in the gastrointestinal lumen, forming an insoluble complex excreted in stool.
drugs.sideEffects: Nausea, constipation or diarrhea, metabolic acidosis, reduced fat-soluble vitamin absorption, rare bowel obstruction
drugs.contraindications: Bowel obstruction, hypophosphatemia, severe gastrointestinal motility disorders
drugs.tooltip: Preferred over calcium acetate when vascular calcification is a concern, because calcium-based binders add to the total calcium burden. Must be taken with meals.

drugs.name: Lisinopril
drugs.primaryEffect: Reduces intraglomerular pressure and proteinuria
drugs.treatmentUsage: Diabetic and nondiabetic proteinuric chronic kidney disease, hypertension, heart failure, post-myocardial infarction
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme, reducing angiotensin II-mediated efferent arteriolar constriction, which lowers intraglomerular pressure and slows glomerular injury.
drugs.sideEffects: Dry cough from bradykinin accumulation, hyperkalemia, angioedema, acute kidney injury in bilateral renal artery stenosis, fetal renal dysgenesis
drugs.contraindications: Pregnancy (boxed warning), bilateral renal artery stenosis, history of angioedema, hyperkalemia, concurrent aliskiren in diabetes
drugs.tooltip: An expected rise in creatinine of up to 30 percent reflects the intended drop in intraglomerular pressure and is not a reason to stop. A larger rise suggests renal artery stenosis.

drugs.name: Losartan
drugs.primaryEffect: Reduces proteinuria and slows chronic kidney disease progression
drugs.treatmentUsage: Diabetic nephropathy, hypertension, heart failure, ACE inhibitor intolerance from cough
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Selectively blocks the angiotensin II type 1 receptor, preventing efferent arteriolar vasoconstriction and aldosterone release without affecting bradykinin metabolism.
drugs.sideEffects: Hyperkalemia, hypotension, acute kidney injury in renal artery stenosis, fetal toxicity; cough and angioedema are much rarer than with ACE inhibitors
drugs.contraindications: Pregnancy (boxed warning), bilateral renal artery stenosis, hyperkalemia, concurrent ACE inhibitor
drugs.tooltip: No cough because bradykinin is not affected — ACE inhibitors cause cough precisely by blocking bradykinin breakdown. Losartan uniquely also has a mild uricosuric effect.

drugs.name: Dapagliflozin
drugs.primaryEffect: Slows chronic kidney disease progression independent of glucose lowering
drugs.treatmentUsage: Chronic kidney disease with albuminuria, heart failure across the ejection fraction spectrum, type 2 diabetes
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Blocks proximal tubule sodium-glucose cotransporter 2, increasing distal sodium delivery which restores tubuloglomerular feedback and reduces intraglomerular hyperfiltration.
drugs.sideEffects: Genital mycotic infection, volume depletion, euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis, initial dip in eGFR, urinary tract infection
drugs.contraindications: Type 1 diabetes, dialysis, recurrent genital infections; hold before major surgery or prolonged fasting
drugs.tooltip: The initial eGFR dip is hemodynamic and expected, reflecting reduced hyperfiltration — long-term decline is markedly slowed. Renal benefit occurs even in patients without diabetes.

drugs.name: Finerenone
drugs.primaryEffect: Reduces renal inflammation and fibrosis
drugs.treatmentUsage: Chronic kidney disease associated with type 2 diabetes to reduce kidney and cardiovascular events
drugs.mechanismOfAction: A nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist with a distinct binding mode that blocks receptor-mediated inflammatory and profibrotic gene transcription more than sodium handling.
drugs.sideEffects: Hyperkalemia, hypotension, decreased eGFR initially; minimal gynecomastia unlike spironolactone
drugs.contraindications: Adrenal insufficiency, concurrent strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, serum potassium above 5.0 at initiation
drugs.tooltip: Distinguished from steroidal antagonists by targeting inflammation and fibrosis more than natriuresis, with less hyperkalemia and no antiandrogen effects. Potassium must be monitored closely.

drugs.name: Sodium Zirconium Cyclosilicate
drugs.primaryEffect: Rapidly lowers serum potassium
drugs.treatmentUsage: Acute and chronic hyperkalemia in chronic kidney disease and heart failure
drugs.mechanismOfAction: A selective inorganic crystalline lattice that traps potassium ions throughout the gastrointestinal tract in exchange for sodium and hydrogen, beginning within one hour.
drugs.sideEffects: Edema from the sodium load, hypokalemia if overdosed, constipation, hypomagnesemia
drugs.contraindications: Bowel obstruction; caution in heart failure and hypertension because of the sodium load; separate from other oral drugs by two hours
drugs.tooltip: Acts faster than patiromer, with onset within an hour, but delivers a sodium load that can worsen volume overload in heart failure. Still not a substitute for calcium in ECG changes.

drugs.name: Cyclophosphamide
drugs.primaryEffect: Profound suppression of B and T lymphocyte function
drugs.treatmentUsage: Severe lupus nephritis, ANCA-associated vasculitis, rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, Goodpasture syndrome, minimal change disease refractory to steroids
drugs.mechanismOfAction: A prodrug activated hepatically to phosphoramide mustard, which cross-links DNA and kills rapidly proliferating lymphocytes, suppressing autoantibody production.
drugs.sideEffects: Hemorrhagic cystitis and bladder cancer from acrolein, myelosuppression, infertility, SIADH, secondary malignancy, infection
drugs.contraindications: Pregnancy, severe bone marrow suppression, active severe infection, urinary outflow obstruction
drugs.tooltip: Mesna binds acrolein in the bladder and prevents hemorrhagic cystitis; aggressive hydration helps too. Rituximab has replaced it in many vasculitis and nephritis protocols.

drugs.name: Tacrolimus
drugs.primaryEffect: Prevents T cell activation and transplant rejection
drugs.treatmentUsage: Prophylaxis of kidney, liver, and heart transplant rejection; membranous nephropathy; minimal change disease; atopic dermatitis topically
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Binds FKBP-12 and the complex inhibits calcineurin, preventing dephosphorylation of NFAT so interleukin-2 transcription and T cell activation do not occur.
drugs.sideEffects: Nephrotoxicity, neurotoxicity with tremor and headache, new-onset diabetes after transplant, hypertension, hyperkalemia, hypomagnesemia, alopecia
drugs.contraindications: Concurrent strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers without level monitoring, hypersensitivity to the castor oil vehicle in intravenous form
drugs.tooltip: Requires therapeutic drug monitoring because of a narrow window and heavy CYP3A4 metabolism. Compared with cyclosporine it causes more diabetes and neurotoxicity but less hirsutism and gum hyperplasia.

drugs.name: Cyclosporine
drugs.primaryEffect: Suppresses T cell-mediated immunity
drugs.treatmentUsage: Transplant rejection prophylaxis, steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome, psoriasis, rheumatoid arthritis, aplastic anemia
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Binds cyclophilin and the complex inhibits calcineurin, preventing NFAT dephosphorylation and thereby blocking interleukin-2 transcription and T cell proliferation.
drugs.sideEffects: Nephrotoxicity, hypertension, gingival hyperplasia, hirsutism, tremor, hyperlipidemia, hyperkalemia, hyperuricemia and gout
drugs.contraindications: Uncontrolled hypertension, significant renal dysfunction, malignancy, concurrent strong CYP3A4 modulators without monitoring
drugs.tooltip: The distinguishing triad from tacrolimus is gingival hyperplasia, hirsutism, and hypertension. Both are nephrotoxic through afferent arteriolar vasoconstriction, which can mimic rejection on biopsy.

drugs.name: Mycophenolate Mofetil
drugs.primaryEffect: Selectively inhibits lymphocyte proliferation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Transplant rejection prophylaxis, lupus nephritis induction and maintenance, ANCA vasculitis maintenance, autoimmune disease
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Its active metabolite inhibits inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase, blocking de novo guanosine synthesis; lymphocytes depend on this pathway because they lack a salvage pathway.
drugs.sideEffects: Diarrhea and gastrointestinal intolerance, leukopenia, anemia, infection including CMV and BK virus, severe teratogenicity, lymphoma risk
drugs.contraindications: Pregnancy (boxed warning for first-trimester loss and congenital malformations), hypersensitivity; requires pregnancy prevention program
drugs.tooltip: Lymphocyte selectivity comes from their exclusive reliance on de novo purine synthesis. It has largely replaced cyclophosphamide for lupus nephritis with equal efficacy and preserved fertility.

drugs.name: Desmopressin (Renal)
drugs.primaryEffect: Concentrates urine and improves platelet function
drugs.treatmentUsage: Central diabetes insipidus, uremic bleeding in advanced kidney disease, nocturnal enuresis, von Willebrand disease
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Selective V2 agonist that inserts aquaporin-2 channels into the collecting duct and also triggers endothelial release of von Willebrand factor, improving platelet adhesion in uremia.
drugs.sideEffects: Hyponatremia and water intoxication, headache, facial flushing, tachyphylaxis after repeated hemostatic dosing
drugs.contraindications: Hyponatremia, primary polydipsia, severe heart failure, creatinine clearance below 50 for some indications
drugs.tooltip: In uremic bleeding, platelet count and coagulation studies are normal but bleeding time is prolonged because uremic toxins impair platelet function. Desmopressin corrects this within an hour.

drugs.name: Fomepizole
drugs.primaryEffect: Blocks formation of toxic alcohol metabolites
drugs.treatmentUsage: Ethylene glycol and methanol poisoning
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Competitively inhibits alcohol dehydrogenase with far higher affinity than ethanol, preventing conversion of ethylene glycol to glycolic and oxalic acid and methanol to formic acid.
drugs.sideEffects: Headache, nausea, dizziness, transient transaminase elevation, injection site reaction
drugs.contraindications: Hypersensitivity; does not remove already-formed metabolites, so dialysis may still be needed
drugs.tooltip: Ethylene glycol causes calcium oxalate crystals and acute kidney injury; methanol causes blindness from retinal formic acid. Both present with high anion gap acidosis and an osmolar gap.

drugs.name: Sodium Thiosulfate
drugs.primaryEffect: Detoxifies cyanide and reduces vascular calcification
drugs.treatmentUsage: Cyanide poisoning including from nitroprusside, calciphylaxis in dialysis patients, prevention of cisplatin ototoxicity
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Provides a sulfur donor for the enzyme rhodanese, which converts cyanide into the far less toxic thiocyanate that is renally excreted.
drugs.sideEffects: Nausea and vomiting, hypotension, metabolic acidosis, thiocyanate accumulation in renal failure, volume overload from the sodium load
drugs.contraindications: Caution in renal impairment because thiocyanate accumulates and causes neurotoxicity
drugs.tooltip: Prolonged high-dose nitroprusside releases cyanide, which is why thiosulfate is co-administered. Hydroxocobalamin is now the preferred first-line cyanide antidote in most settings.

drugs.name: Cinacalcet (Renal)
drugs.primaryEffect: Suppresses parathyroid hormone in secondary hyperparathyroidism
drugs.treatmentUsage: Secondary hyperparathyroidism in dialysis patients, parathyroid carcinoma, refractory primary hyperparathyroidism
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Allosteric activator of the parathyroid calcium-sensing receptor that increases its sensitivity to extracellular calcium, suppressing PTH synthesis and secretion.
drugs.sideEffects: Hypocalcemia with paresthesias and tetany, nausea and vomiting, QT prolongation, adynamic bone disease
drugs.contraindications: Serum calcium below the normal range; requires frequent calcium and PTH monitoring
drugs.tooltip: Unlike vitamin D analogs, it lowers PTH without raising calcium and phosphate, which is its main advantage in the CKD mineral bone disorder algorithm.

drugs.name: Norepinephrine
drugs.primaryEffect: Restores mean arterial pressure and renal perfusion in shock
drugs.treatmentUsage: Septic shock (first-line vasopressor), cardiogenic and other vasodilatory shock, hepatorenal syndrome in the ICU
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Potent alpha-1 adrenergic agonist causing arterial and venous vasoconstriction with modest beta-1 inotropic effect, raising systemic vascular resistance and perfusion pressure.
drugs.sideEffects: Peripheral and mesenteric ischemia, reflex bradycardia, arrhythmias, tissue necrosis with extravasation, hyperglycemia
drugs.contraindications: Uncorrected hypovolemia; caution with peripheral vascular disease; extravasation is treated with phentolamine
drugs.tooltip: Restoring perfusion pressure protects the kidney in septic shock, contrary to the old fear that vasopressors worsen renal ischemia. Low-dose dopamine for renal protection has been disproven.

drugs.name: Hydroxocobalamin
drugs.primaryEffect: Binds and neutralizes circulating cyanide
drugs.treatmentUsage: Cyanide poisoning from smoke inhalation, nitroprusside toxicity, or ingestion; refractory vasoplegic shock
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Binds cyanide with high affinity to form cyanocobalamin (vitamin B12), which is nontoxic and renally excreted, and additionally scavenges nitric oxide.
drugs.sideEffects: Red discoloration of skin, urine, and plasma that interferes with colorimetric lab assays and dialysis machines; hypertension; rash; anaphylaxis
drugs.contraindications: Known hypersensitivity; no absolute contraindication in life-threatening cyanide toxicity
drugs.tooltip: Preferred over nitrite-based kits in smoke inhalation because it does not induce methemoglobinemia, which would be catastrophic in a patient who also has carbon monoxide poisoning.
